gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-samarit: Noto Sans Samaritan reads friendly and sturdy, its hefty lowercase holding generous daylight inside every curve while Disorder shouts above it. Long paragraphs would feel easygoing.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-saurash: Clean and level-headed, Noto Sans Saurashtra keeps its capitals close to the lowercase height and its counters open to the outside. But Disorder, with crossbars as thick as its stems, supplies the rough noise that this sans lacks.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-sc: Disorder draws every terminal at the width it started with, giving the heading a raw, unmodulated stamp. And Noto Sans SC follows in modern sans-serif calm, its curves stopping short, so paragraphs would flow quietly beneath.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Disorder's t has crossbar and stem in matching weight. Noto Sans Sharada, with bulky lowercase and open c forms, can take a smaller size in the text so the heading stays the loudest thing there.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Rough, wide-spaced, unmodulated. Noto Sans Soyombo sits below with a sizable x-height and curves that stay open, so a long page of it would read smoothly on a screen.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-sundane: Noto Sans Sundanese reads clean and level, with open-mouthed e crossbars and capitals barely above the lowercase. And over many paragraphs it would stay out of the way, which leaves Disorder's fixed-pen strokes to do the shouting.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac reads approachable and modern, its lowercase bowls round like blown glass bulbs and its s turns wide and easy. Noto Sans Syriac would carry a long page gently, while Disorder's router-cut strokes stay up top.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-syriac-: Approachable and contemporary, Noto Sans Syriac Eastern pairs lofty lowercase with small capitals and curve endings kept well apart. Disorder is the rough shouter; this body is the patient talker.
